claims.claim: The work was written in A.D. 156.
The work was addressed to the Christian community at Philomelium in Greater Phrygia and to all the congregations of the Holy and Catholic Church in every place.
The work was written to report on the martyrs and especially the blessed Polycarp, who put an end to the persecution by his martyrdom, setting a seal upon it.

The work was written so that the Lord might show from above a martyrdom becoming the Gospel, and that readers might become followers of Christ's example, having regard not merely to themselves but also to their neighbours.
The work is the oldest detailed extant account of the arrest and martyrdom of a single individual.
The work provides the earliest evidence for the cult of martyrs, including relics, distinguished from worship due to Christ.
Polycarp was Bishop of Smyrna and lived approximately from A.D. 69 to 155.
Polycarp was a disciple of John the Apostle, according to Irenaeus and Tertullian.
Polycarp was arrested after being sought by authorities, initially staying in the city but then departing to a country house not far distant from the city.
Three days before he was taken, Polycarp had a vision in which the pillow under his head seemed on fire, and he prophesied that he must be burnt alive.
